svg.text: STAFFING A WARD: SKILL MIX BEATS HEAD COUNT
Six people who cannot give an intravenous drug are not the same as four who can.
WHAT DETERMINES HOW MANY NURSES A WARD NEEDS

g.text: Patient dependency, not bed numbers · turnover of admissions and discharges · ward layout and distance
Skill mix and who may legally do what · leave, study and sickness · teaching and student supervision load
A twenty-bed ward of stable convalescents and a twenty-bed ward of ventilated patients are not the same ward.
Put an experienced nurse on every shift.
Apply the same rule to yourself.
Prioritise, do not simply work faster.
Name what will not be done today.
Escalate in writing, before the harm.
Silent absorption of a shortage tells
Replacing a trained nurse costs far more than retaining one: recruitment, orientation, months of reduced output,
and the experience that walked out with her. Retention is a financial strategy, not a kindness.
Nurses rarely leave because of money alone. They leave supervisors.
Recognition, a predictable roster, a route to training and being listened to cost the budget almost nothing.
